propositions: Patch-set uploads that fail to vote within a single reconciler pass are permanently excluded from future reconciliation windows because the cursor advances unconditionally to the newest event time without tracking which candidates were never voted.

A webhook delivery failure to an upload event leaves no recovery path because the Gerrit webhooks plugin is at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), the receiver 202-ACKs into a volatile queue, and the reconciler skips any candidate that fell outside its window.

Three distinct reconciler paths (reconcile_check_error, review_timeout, voter deferred/error) continue without voting but the persisted cursor still advances to newest, so those candidates are never re-driven despite explicit contracts promising retry on next pass.

The guarding test is a false green because its fake events-log records the since parameter but ignores it, returning the full event list regardless, so the production cursor filter behavior is never exercised.
Manual nudges (recheck-review comment or no-op rebase) revive a stalled change by minting a new events-log event with a timestamp after the cursor, re-admitting the change to the reconciler window.
Queue depth and backfill backlog are invisible to operators, making it impossible to distinguish between a bot down, review in progress, queued behind N, and permanently dropped states.
